chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, saying: Hamid ibn Ziyad al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Maythami, from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Isma'il, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Shall I show you the shirt of the Qaim that he will rise in?" I said: "Yes." He then called for a container, opened it, and took out a shirt made of coarse fabric. He unfolded it, and there was blood on its left sleeve. He said: "This is the shirt of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), which he was wearing on the day his tooth was struck, and it is with this shirt that the Qaim will rise." I kissed the blood and placed it on my face. Then Abu Abdullah folded the shirt and put it away.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdullah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qaim (the Awaited Imam), a title for the Mahdi
key_terms.رَبَاعِيَتُهُ: His tooth (specifically the upper front tooth)
key_terms.قَمَطَرٌ: A container or box for storing items
key_terms.قَمِيصٌ كَرَابِيسَ: A shirt made of coarse fabric (karrabisa)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the shirt shown by Imam al-Sadiq regarding the Qaim?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) presents the shirt of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), stained with blood from the fracture of his tooth (rubāʿiyya), as the specific garment in which the Qaim (the Awaited Imam) will rise. This narrative underscores the Shia concept of *tawassul* through physical relics (*athar*) and establishes a tangible, hereditary link between the Prophet’s suffering and the eschatological mission of the Mahdi, reinforcing the continuity of the Imamate.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: 42 - Muhammad b. Hammam narrated to us, saying: Hamid b. Ziyad al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan b. Muhammad b. Sama'ah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad b. al-Hasan al-Maythami, from his uncle al-Husayn b. Isma'il, from Ya'qub b. Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said: "Shall I show you the shirt of the Qaim that he will rise in?" I said: "Yes."

He then called for a container, opened it, and took out a shirt made of coarse fabric. He unfolded it, and there was blood on its left sleeve. He said: "This is the shirt of the Messenger of Allah (saw), which he was wearing on the day his tooth was struck, and it is with this shirt that the Qaim will rise." 

I kissed the blood and placed it on my face. Then Abu Abdullah folded the shirt and put it away.
